newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: svc-ABN AMRO aims for top of global banking leaque.
newsitem.headline: svc-ABN AMRO aims for top of global banking leaque.

text.p: ABN AMRO has spent years carving a role outside the small Dutch banking market and its proposed $1.9 billion offer for Standard Federal Bank of the United States is its biggest acquisition to date.

Formed in a 1990 merger, ABN AMRO has grown through acquisitions into the biggest foreign bank in the U.S. and has 550 offices in over 60 countries -- winning the right to be called one of Europe's genuinely global banks.
The 1992 purchase of British stockbroker Hoare Govett revealed ambitions to grow as an integrated commercial and investment bank. But this goal has proved elusive.

ABN AMRO won the lucrative stewardship of the Netherland's largest share flotation, when the state sold a third of Dutch telecoms giant PTT for 6.9 billion guilders ($4.34 billion), but still struggled to win a seat at merchant banking's top table.
ABN AMRO has a track record of predatory moves in banking -- it made no secret of its keen interest in collapsed U.K. merchant bank Barings which was snapped up by arch-rival ING last year.

It has been more successful in the U.S. where it acquired the Illinois bank, LaSalle National Corp in 1979. Other U.S. acquisitions include, Lane Financial, 1987; Exchange Bancorp, 1990; Talman, 1992; Cragin, 1994; Comerica Illinois, 1996 and Columbia National Bank, 1996.
LaSalle mainly operates in the Chicago area where it has 130 branches and 7,750 staff.
